memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And there was evening, and there was morning—the third day. - Gen 1:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This short verse closes the third day of creation. On its own it seems simple, almost like a full stop at the end of a sentence. But it carries a quiet beauty worth pausing over. God has finished another day of good work, and He marks it with that steady rhythm we keep hearing: "there was evening, and there was morning."

There is faithfulness in this repetition. Day after day, God works, completes, and moves forward. Nothing is left half-done. He does not grow tired, distracted, or discouraged. Each day He finishes what He set out to do. The God who completed the third day is the God who completes everything He begins.

This is a great comfort for us. Sometimes our own lives feel unfinished, full of loose ends, half-formed hopes, and work still in progress. But we serve a God who finishes His work. He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion (Phil 1:6). Your growth, your healing, your walk with Him, none of it is abandoned.

And the same steady rhythm of evening and morning still governs our days, reminding us that God is ordering time itself. Each new morning is His mercy; each evening, His invitation to rest. Trust the God who completes every day, and every good work He has begun in you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What unfinished area of your life do you need to entrust to the God who completes His work?
2. How can the rhythm of evening and morning remind you of God's faithfulness today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You finish everything You begin. Thank You that the good work You started in me will be completed by You. Help me rest in that assurance today. Amen.
